correctness.rationale: For the uniform 8-digit ternary carpet, the Fourier digit mask is exactly M(x,y)=exp(-2 pi i(x+y))[(1+2cos2pi x)(1+2cos2pi y)-1]/8. Removing all common powers of 3 reduces each nonzero integer frequency to a primitive pair, with first mask modulus 1/8. Checked the two pointwise sharp bounds for subsequent masks: for one coordinate primitive, c_j=(3s(3^-j)-1)/8, for both primitive b_j=(s(3^-j)^2-1)/8; all equality congruences force ±axis-unit or ±diagonal-unit residues at every power of 3. At the first incompatible ternary digit, one-coordinate-primitive nonextremizers have a mask <=1/2, hence coefficient <=1/16. The explicit infinite-product bound B>515/7776>1/16 separates the second family from all others; c_j>b_j yields A>B. Independently evaluated mask and convergent products: A≈0.1007268724734242, B≈0.08075493227479424; (2,0) is below 1/16; (3,0) reproduces A. Cyclotomic reduction ζ→1 mod(3,ζ-1) sends each numerator to 8≡-1 mod3, ensuring nonzero factors, with summable tail guaranteeing a nonzero product. Thus all integer Fourier multipliers are nonzero, giving the sharp first and second L² convolution norm levels and injectivity; finite artifact checks alone do not establish the unbounded frequency assertion.
